description: Coverage accounting. 'quarantine' lists tests that no CI leg executes, each with an owner, a review date and the gap it leaves; the Safety evidence job fails on any other never-executed test. 'dispositions' explain removed or weakened coverage; check_coverage_regression.py accepts only dispositions added by the same change. See docs/rules/safety-evidence.md.

quarantine.reason: Collation.Default snapshots the culture once per process, so the test passes only as the first LiteDB use in the process; after another test created a database it sees that culture instead of 'fi'.
quarantine.gap: A new database taking its collation from the current thread culture is not asserted on any CI leg; product behaviour (process-wide snapshot) decides whether the test can be made order-independent.

quarantine.reason: Not supported yet: rebuilding 'ana'/'ANA' from en-US/None to en-US/IgnoreCase throws 'Cannot insert duplicate key' instead of recording the collision in _rebuild_errors.
quarantine.gap: Rebuilding to a collation under which unique keys collide is not exercised; the expected _rebuild_errors behaviour is not implemented.

quarantine.reason: Takes ~102 s (100 iterations with a 1 s sleep; passed 5/5 locally on net10.0). The DiskWriterQueue race of #2127 no longer exists; the queue was removed in 198f0a672.
quarantine.gap: Back-to-back file-backed inserts into 100 recreated databases do not run in CI; the original race cannot recur, so the test is a candidate to retire as obsolete.

dispositions.invariant: Every test leg's results are uploaded and judged; no existing timeout, filter or partition changes.
dispositions.reason: Adds the Safety policy and Safety evidence jobs (10-minute limits) and a results upload for the .NET Framework leg, which uploaded nothing before; existing test steps keep their timeouts and filters.

dispositions.invariant: A checkpoint on a log that answers "cannot sync" never loses a commit and keeps writing; it retries the log sync and drains the WAL once the log syncs.
dispositions.reason: Decision D and implementation note 12: no in-place overwrite behind a recovery copy that is only in the OS cache. With durable commits off, such a checkpoint now writes nothing and keeps the WAL (it used to overwrite data in write order); with durable commits on, the commit fails before it writes (decision 3). The new tests assert byte-identical files, kept frames, the drain once the log syncs and power-loss images.

dispositions.invariant: Storage that cannot sync never reuses retired WAL slots, and a snapshot checkpoint there keeps the reader's snapshot and every commit.
dispositions.reason: Decision 3 splits the scenario by mode: without durable commits it still appends instead of reusing slots; with durable commits the commit on that log now fails loudly before it writes.

dispositions.invariant: A shared connection on a log that cannot sync reports it after later operations reopen engines, and fresh shared engines never reuse slots retired there.
dispositions.reason: Decisions 3, 6 and 13: with durable commits the commit fails, the failure is kept connection-wide and the connection shows only acknowledged commits; without durable commits "cannot sync" is no failure (default A) and slots are still never reused. The scenario is now asserted per mode.

dispositions.invariant: A database on a log that never syncs stays readable with every committed row, and no format change tears its header.
dispositions.reason: Implementation note 12 and decisions 2, 3 and D: an index migration, a 5.x conversion or a compact promotion overwrites the header behind a journal the log cannot make durable, so it is refused before it writes: the open falls back to read-only, and a compact write stores BSON instead. With durable commits the commit fails before it writes. They used to publish the new format behind an OS-cached journal.

dispositions.invariant: Log storage that rejects sync never corrupts data, a commit is never acknowledged as durable when it is not, and an opted-out checkpoint makes the log durable before it overwrites data.
dispositions.reason: Decisions 3 and D: with durable commits a log that cannot sync fails the commit (before it writes, or with outcome unknown when it stops syncing after the frames reached the OS) instead of degrading silently; without durable commits it degrades and a checkpoint writes nothing behind it. The opted-out checkpoint's sync order gained the data sync first (a checkpoint writes only to a data file that just synced), so that test was renamed with the new order.

dispositions.invariant: A WAL directory that cannot sync is reported and never loses a commit acknowledged as durable.
dispositions.reason: Decision 9: with durable commits such a directory fails the commit before it writes; without durable commits it keeps committing and reports the log as not durable.

dispositions.invariant: After a disk-full write failure the instance explains how to recover and never writes again until reopened.
dispositions.reason: Decision 6 and default B: a write failure is recorded and the engine continues read-only (reads keep working) instead of closing; the record names the file.

dispositions.invariant: LiteDatabase(Stream) checkpoints each commit into the caller's stream and leaves the persisted checkpoint pragma as it was.
dispositions.reason: The stream constructor no longer persists CHECKPOINT=1 at all (a 5.0.21 regression fixed in this PR), so the test asserts the pragma never changes, that a commit reaches the stream, and that it is still 1000 after disposal.

dispositions.invariant: A damaged file opened with AutoRebuild is detected (INVALID_DATAFILE_STATE) and recovered with every document.
dispositions.reason: AutoRebuild now rebuilds in the same open that detects the damage (5.0.21 behaviour for damaged 5.0.21 files), so the first open no longer throws error 999; the removed assertions checked that throw. Each test now asserts the rebuild's backup file exists and the full recovered counts.

dispositions.invariant: Durable commits on storage that cannot sync, and the opted-out checkpoint's barriers.
dispositions.reason: The two tolerance tests of this file (see 3027-durable-commits-log-cannot-sync) moved to the per-mode tests of CheckpointDurability_Tests, NativeFileSync_Tests and OverwriteBarrier_Tests; one assertion call fewer remains here.

dispositions.invariant: Every index-migration recovery case runs to completion and checks its oracle.
dispositions.reason: The harness now reports how far a case got when it times out (the phase reached), for diagnosis; no case, oracle or timeout changed.

dispositions.invariant: Every .NET Framework test runs to completion and reports on each CI run.
dispositions.reason: The net481 job was cancelled at its 20-minute limit after 4713 tests ran without a failure: the durability suites grew. 30 minutes lets the whole leg finish; the .NET jobs allow 40. No filter, partition or test changed.

dispositions.invariant: A WAL directory that cannot sync degrades visibly and never loses an acknowledged commit.
dispositions.reason: The evidence test was split by mode (decision 9, see 3027-wal-directory-cannot-sync); the registry names both new tests.
